# skcode - The Sovereign Coding Client

> Where you code by hand. The interactive, human-facing coding client of the SKWorld stack -
> a thin client of the skharness engine, never a second engine. Its read-only remote session
> plane ships today (skcode-hostd, P0); interactive Code + Dispatch is on the roadmap. GPL-3.0.

skcode is one of three names in the SKWorld coding stack, and the boundary between them is the
point (ADR-0001). One engine, two front doors:

- **skos** (skos.skworld.io) - the operator OS. It knows you: GTD, memory, coord board, ITIL,
  scheduler, the AI-operator seat. It decides what and why to build.
- **skharness** (skharness.skworld.io) - the autocode engine. The one loop: assess → build →
  grade → twin-gate (score==5 + CI + coverage) → finalize/merge. Input: a repo + a task.
  Output: a reviewed PR. Knows only the repo and the task, runs in isolated sandboxes.
- **skcode** (skcode.skworld.io) - the coding client. The interactive surface where a human codes
  by hand. It invokes skharness for autonomous builds rather than growing its own loop. It holds
  session-scoped context (the open project), never the operator's full personal graph.

The one-line rule: **skos knows you. skharness builds code. skcode is where you code by hand.**

## Honest status (this is important)

skcode is REAL, delivered today as a DISTRIBUTED feature. There is NO standalone skcode package
or repo yet - the code lives across three repos that already ship:

- **skcode host daemon (session plane) - SHIPPED, P0 read-only MVP.** Lives INSIDE skharness by
  deliberate design ("skcode's host daemon IS skharness, promoted and hardened"). Entry point
  `skcode-hostd` (= `skharness.serve:main`), binds a Tailscale IP only on port 9394, capauth-gated
  with audience `skcode`, systemd unit `skcode-hostd.service`, 36 tests. It is the "session plane"
  of the two-plane Harness: the task plane is autocode, the session plane is skcode remote session
  control. Read-only: list live agent sessions and stream one; no inject, spawn, or kill exists
  (POST/DELETE return 405, by design).
- **Flutter client pane - SHIPPED (Grade B).** A "Code" pane in skchat-app
  (`lib/features/skcode/`) embeds the hostd web client same-origin over the 443 funnel.
- **Operator adapter - SHIPPED.** `skcapstone/operator_seat/skcode_adapter.py`; Atlas (the
  AI-operator seat) watches and steers hostd (health, archive stale session, restart, pause dispatch).

STILL ON THE ROADMAP: interactive Code + Dispatch (P2) - spawn and steer sessions, with a gated
dispatch that calls `skharness.autocode.ratify` (a thin call into the engine, never a re-forked loop).

## Architecture

skcode is a thin client of skharness, not a second engine. skharness became a TWO-PLANE Harness:

- **Task plane** - autocode. A repo + a brief become a reviewed PR in an isolated Docker sandbox.
- **Session plane** - skcode. Remote control over live agent sessions over a PTY + tmux backing.

Two separate Harness classes on one ABC, so turning on the session plane never touches the frozen
autocode adapter. skcode's daemon is skharness promoted and hardened; the engine is untouched.

## The phase ladder

| Phase | Deliverable | Gate |
|-------|-------------|------|
| P0 (DONE) | Read-only Code: list + stream, capauth-gated, one device, sandbox scope. | skharness P0 + a paired device. |
| P1 (next) | Input injection (text/voice/file), manual/auto toggle, per-session model switch, rename/archive/share. | Unified resolver + dynamic catalog; authz.decide frozen. |
| P2 (Dispatch) | Spawn & steer a new session; gated dispatch → skharness.autocode.ratify; mandatory RCE guards. | capauth.pairing (M2) + authz.decide (M3) + repo allowlist. |
| P3 (Fleet) | Pi + opencode adapters; harness switch = fork/re-spawn; fleet roll; cross-host merge; skcoord card store. | Pi spike + fleet install; skcoord extraction. |
| P4 (Off-tailnet + shell) | skcomms stream_channel for cellular attach; skcode as a Grade A shell module. | Shell phase + skcomms stream seam. |

## Security posture

skcode is remote code execution on your own hosts, so it is security-first from P0: Tailscale-only
binding (refuses 0.0.0.0 and public Funnel ports), capauth-gated and fail-closed (audience `skcode`),
read-only P0 (the write surface does not exist yet), least-privilege by construction (a sandbox
session gets no SKAGENT / sk* MCP / memory - enforced by not wiring the modules), and P2 RCE guards
(argv-only subprocess, repo allowlist, name charset limits, git-worktree isolation, prompt-as-data).
